snippet.title: What Happens If Iran Closes the Strait of Hormuz? 🌍💥
snippet.description:
If Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz, it could trigger a massive global energy crisis. This narrow waterway is one of the world’s most strategic chokepoints, where roughly 20% of the planet’s oil and gas passes through. A closure would immediately disrupt energy supplies, spike oil prices, and affect economies worldwide.

In this 10-second short, we break down the potential consequences:

Oil & Gas Flow: 20% of global energy supply is at risk.

Price Shock: Oil prices could skyrocket overnight.

Global Markets: Stock markets could react negatively to energy instability.

Economic Impact: Countries dependent on Middle Eastern oil would feel the pinch first.

Energy Security: Nations may scramble to secure alternative energy routes.

Understanding this helps you grasp why geopolitical tensions in the Middle East can impact everyone — not just the region itself.

snippet.title: Why Iran & The US Have Hated Each Other Since 1979
snippet.description:
Why are Iran and the United States still enemies after more than four decades?

It all began with the Iranian Revolution in 1979. The revolution overthrew the Western-backed Shah and brought Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini to power. Soon after, Iranian students stormed the U.S. Embassy in Tehran during the Iran Hostage Crisis, holding 52 Americans hostage for 444 days.

The crisis humiliated President Jimmy Carter and shattered diplomatic relations between the two nations.

Since then, tensions have continued through:

U.S. economic sanctions

Proxy conflicts in the Middle East

Disputes over Iran’s nuclear program

The 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (nuclear deal)

The U.S. withdrawal under Donald Trump

Today, the rivalry shapes politics across the Middle East and continues to influence global security.

This short breaks down how a single revolutionary moment in 1979 created one of the longest-running geopolitical conflicts in modern history.
